title: From price list to drawer: surviving commercial slide sets and cabinets as reverse trade archives
research_problem: Trade catalogues describe what makers offered. Surviving cabinets show what buyers actually accumulated, retained, replaced, mixed and relabelled. The strongest research route is therefore bidirectional: catalogue → possible object and surviving label → targeted catalogue row.
working_claim: A commercial microscope slide did not cease to be a commodity when purchased. Maker labels, series numbers, subject titles, secondary retailer labels and cabinet position could preserve or rewrite parts of its commercial identity through later private and institutional custody. Mixed cabinets are therefore transaction residues, not merely taxonomic collections.

recommended_reverse_workflow: 1. Photograph/transcribe every visible label before searching catalogues.
2. Preserve maker label, retailer/secondary label, subject, locality, date and number as separate fields.
3. Search exact label wording against maker catalogues and advertisements; record zero/one/multiple candidate rows.
4. Only after a catalogue match, compare physical format, preparation method, price/grade language and series position.
5. Record cabinet position independently from maker/series number: cabinet order is a later address unless proven original.
6. Use missing, replaced, broken or foreign-maker slides as evidence of cabinet maintenance rather than silently excluding them.
7. Distinguish maker, preparer, wholesaler, retailer and collector even when labels collapse them.

research_payoff.trade_article: Instead of reconstructing a market solely from catalogues and advertisements, use surviving cabinets to show what commercial identities remained materially attached to purchased slides and how private/institutional storage recomposed makers into new collections.
research_payoff.valuation_question: Price and quality categories can be tested against surviving physical formats only where a specific catalogue row or maker-grade system is securely matched.
research_payoff.circulation_question: Secondary labels and maker mixtures can reveal retail and resale channels that are invisible in the maker's own catalogue.
research_payoff.key_guard: A slide found in a later cabinet proves later co-presence, not a single nineteenth-century purchase event.
